title: Napoleon crowns himself Emperor
summary: In Notre-Dame de Paris, in the presence of Pope Pius VII, Napoleon crowns himself Emperor of the French and then crowns Josephine. His elevation to emperor had been approved in a referendum.

title: Battle of Trafalgar
summary: Nelson's British fleet destroys the combined French and Spanish fleets; Nelson is killed. Britain rules the waves for a century.

title: Battle of Austerlitz
summary: Napoleon's masterpiece: he defeats the Russian and Austrian emperors. The Holy Roman Empire is dissolved the following year.

title: Britain abolishes the slave trade
summary: After 18 years of attempts, Parliament passes an act prohibiting the Atlantic slave trade in the British Empire. It does not free those already enslaved; slavery remains legal in most of the Empire until the Slavery Abolition Act of 1833.

title: Latin American wars of independence begin
summary: From 1810, after Napoleon's invasion of Spain broke up the Spanish Crown, wars of independence spread across Spain's American empire. Leaders such as Simón Bolívar and Agustín de Iturbide fight to build new states, and the wars end with independent nations across the Americas.

title: Napoleon in Moscow
summary: Napoleon's Grande Armée of over 600,000 reaches a burning, abandoned Moscow. Its retreat through the Russian winter destroys it.

title: Battle of Waterloo
summary: Wellington and Blücher defeat Napoleon for the last time. He is exiled to St Helena.

title: Congress of Vienna
summary: The great powers redraw Europe's map after Napoleon, restore monarchies and create a 'Concert of Europe' that prevents a general war for a century.

title: Eruption of Mount Tambora
summary: The most powerful eruption in recorded history kills tens of thousands and causes the 'Year Without a Summer' (1816) with crop failures across the Northern Hemisphere.

title: Greek War of Independence
summary: Greeks rise against Ottoman rule; with British, French and Russian help (Navarino, 1827) they win an independent kingdom in 1830.

title: First inter-city railway
summary: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opens, with Stephenson's locomotives — the start of the railway age.

title: First Opium War
summary: Britain goes to war when China tries to stop the opium trade. The Treaty of Nanking cedes Hong Kong — the start of China's 'century of humiliation'.

title: Great Irish Famine
summary: Potato blight and British policy cause the death of about a million people and the emigration of another million.

title: Revolutions of 1848
summary: Revolutions sweep Europe from Paris to Vienna, Berlin, Milan and Budapest, demanding constitutions and national unity. Most are crushed within a year, but serfdom ends in Austria.

title: The Communist Manifesto
summary: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels publish their pamphlet calling on the workers of the world to unite.

title: Taiping Rebellion
summary: A rebel movement led by a man who believed himself the brother of Jesus builds a state centred on Nanjing; the war kills perhaps 20–30 million people.

title: Perry's 'black ships' arrive in Japan
summary: Warships of the US Navy under Commodore Matthew Perry arrive to force an end to Japan's 220-year-old policy of isolation and open its ports to American trade. The expedition leads to diplomatic relations with the Western powers and eventually to the fall of the Tokugawa shogunate and the restoration of the Emperor.

title: Crimean War
summary: Britain, France and the Ottomans fight Russia; Florence Nightingale's nursing reforms and the first war photography come out of it.

title: Indian Rebellion of 1857
summary: Indian soldiers in the East India Company's army mutiny and the revolt spreads. After it is crushed, the British Crown takes direct rule (the Raj).

title: Darwin's On the Origin of Species
summary: Charles Darwin sets out the theory of evolution by natural selection.

title: Kingdom of Italy proclaimed
summary: After Garibaldi's conquest of the south, Victor Emmanuel II becomes king of a united Italy. Venice joins in 1866, Rome in 1870.

title: Russia frees the serfs
summary: Alexander II's Emancipation Reform frees some 23 million privately held serfs.

title: Battle of Gettysburg
summary: The bloodiest battle of the American Civil War, with over 50,000 casualties, ends when Union general George Meade's army defeats Robert E. Lee's Confederate army and halts its invasion of the North. It is widely considered the turning point of the war.

title: Meiji Restoration
summary: The shogunate is overthrown and power restored to the Emperor Meiji. Japan industrialises at astonishing speed and becomes a great power within 40 years.

title: Suez Canal opens
summary: The canal linking the Mediterranean and Red Sea cuts the voyage from Europe to Asia by thousands of kilometres and becomes one of the world's most strategic waterways.

title: German Empire proclaimed
summary: After defeating France, Bismarck's Prussia unites Germany; Wilhelm I is proclaimed Kaiser at Versailles.

title: First telephone call
summary: Alexander Graham Bell calls his assistant: 'Mr Watson, come here — I want to see you.'

title: Practical electric light bulb
summary: Thomas Edison's lab demonstrates a long-lasting carbon-filament bulb; electric power networks follow within a few years.

title: Berlin Conference
summary: European powers set rules for claiming African territory. Within 30 years almost the whole continent is colonised — only Ethiopia and Liberia remain independent.

title: Eruption of Krakatoa
summary: The volcanic island of Krakatoa explodes and collapses into a caldera; one explosion is the loudest sound in recorded history, heard 4,800 km away in Perth. At least 36,417 deaths are attributed to the eruption and its tsunamis.

title: Battle of Adwa
summary: Emperor Menelik II's Ethiopian army decisively defeats an Italian invasion force, preserving Ethiopia's independence.

title: Boxer Rebellion
summary: An anti-foreign movement besieges the foreign legations in Beijing; an eight-nation army crushes it.

title: First powered flight
summary: Orville and Wilbur Wright fly a powered, controlled aeroplane for 12 seconds.

title: Battle of Tsushima
summary: Japan's navy annihilates the Russian Baltic Fleet — the first defeat of a European great power by an Asian one in modern times.

title: Einstein's 'miracle year'
summary: A patent clerk publishes papers on special relativity, E = mc², light quanta and Brownian motion, transforming physics.

title: Xinhai Revolution
summary: An uprising in Wuchang topples the Qing dynasty. China becomes a republic in 1912, ending over 2,000 years of imperial rule.

title: Sinking of the Titanic
summary: The 'unsinkable' liner hits an iceberg on her maiden voyage; over 1,500 people die.

title: Mexican Revolution
summary: A revolt against the dictator Porfirio Díaz becomes a decade of civil war involving Pancho Villa and Emiliano Zapata.
